proposed_errata.before_evidence: Patella tendon: Complete rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with 1.5-2 cm retracted tendon gap and intervening fluid/hematoma formation. Underlying severe patellar tendinosis. Osseous fragments are embedded within the retracted patellar tendon fibers.
proposed_errata.source_quote:
Indication: Gym injury one week prior.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Femorotibial alignment is anatomic. Avulsive fragmentation of inferior patellar enthesophytes with some reactive marrow edema in the inferior patella. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Irregularity of the distal quadriceps tendon, most likely sequelae of laxity due to patella alta, possibly with some mild underlying tendinosis.
Patella tendon: Complete rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with 1.5-2 cm retracted tendon gap and intervening fluid/hematoma formation. Underlying severe patellar tendinosis. Osseous fragments are embedded within the retracted patellar tendon fibers.
proposed_errata.reason: I retain uncertain against the first reader positive. Recent gym injury, current tendon rupture/hematoma and avulsive enthesophyte fragmentation make acute bone injury plausible, but the age/current fracture status of the osseous fragments is not itself expressly established. I would mask this report-derived target pending root adjudication, preserving both readers and the existing positive; I do not diagnose a different fracture.
